leads.title: Chlorpromazine and antipsychotic drugs in France
leads.why: The first antipsychotic emptied mental hospitals across the world within two decades and opened the search for antidepressants and the chemistry of the brain.
leads.verify: The 1950 synthesis at Rhone-Poulenc, Laborit's observations and the 1952 trials by Delay and Deniker; the speed of adoption; the effect on hospital populations.
search: chlorpromazine deinstitutionalization history Healy Creation of Psychopharmacology

leads.title: Maritime quarantine in the Adriatic
leads.why: Plague-era port cities set up isolation periods, pesthouses and health boards, the first standing public machinery against epidemics.
leads.verify: The text and date of the 1377 Ragusan decree; the first permanent lazaretto (Venice, 1423) and health magistracy; earlier isolation practices for leprosy and in the Islamic world.
search: origins of quarantine Emerging Infectious Diseases

leads.title: Trepanation in Neolithic Europe
leads.where: Western and central Europe (Ensisheim, Alsace, and later sites)
leads.why: Healed skull openings across Neolithic Europe show that stone-tool surgeons operated on the head and that most patients lived.
leads.verify: The earliest securely dated healed trepanation (Ensisheim, and the earlier claims from Vasilyevka in Ukraine and Taforalt in Morocco); survival rates; the reasons proposed for the operation.

leads.title: Trepanation in the Andes
leads.where: South coast and highlands of Peru
leads.why: Andean surgeons opened skulls for some two thousand years, and by Inka times most of their patients survived.
leads.verify: The earliest dated Andean trepanations (Paracas) and the techniques used; survival rates by period; the link to head wounds from warfare.
search: Verano Holes in the Head trepanation ancient Peru

leads.title: Herbal general anaesthesia in Japan
leads.why: A drink compounded from datura and aconite let Hanaoka Seishu and his pupils remove breast tumours from unconscious patients four decades before ether.
leads.verify: The date and documentation of the first operation under tsusensan; the formula and its sources in Chinese and Dutch medicine; how far the method spread through his school and why it was not carried on.

leads.title: Lacquer coating in Neolithic China
leads.where: Lower Yangtze (Kuahuqiao and Hemudu, Zhejiang), China
leads.why: Lacquer became East Asia's waterproof, durable coating for vessels, furniture, armour and coffins, and a major craft industry for seven thousand years.
leads.verify: Pin down the earliest lacquered objects in China (the Kuahuqiao bow, the Hemudu red bowl) and compare with the Jomon finds at Kakinoshima, Hokkaido, claimed at c. 7000 BCE. Establish whether specialists regard Chinese and Japanese lacquer as independent and which is first; Jomon lacquer may need its own record.

concepts.name: Lacquer
concepts.summary: Coating wood, fibre or other bodies with refined tree sap that cures to a hard, waterproof film.

concepts.name: Drug treatment of mental illness
concepts.summary: Relieving the symptoms of a major mental illness with a drug that acts on them specifically, not by sedation alone.

concepts.name: Quarantine
concepts.summary: Holding arriving people, ships and goods apart for a fixed period so that an epidemic disease cannot enter.

concepts.name: Surgical general anaesthesia
concepts.summary: Medical approaches that produce a reversible anaesthetic state for surgery.

concepts.name: Trepanation
concepts.summary: Cutting an opening in the skull of a living person who then survives.
